about.append: People add replies below: attendance, ideas, a log.
about.blocks: Type /spoiler for a part that opens on click, or /pin for a part locked with a PIN. Handy for answers or passwords in a shared note.
about.burn: A note can delete itself after it’s opened, or after a set time. Link previews in chat apps don’t count.
about.check: The text is locked, but the checklist can be ticked. For shopping lists or team routines.
about.clip: Drag this button to your bookmarks bar. On any page, select some text and click the bookmark: a new note opens with the title, address and selection. They travel in the # part of the link, so the server doesn't see them until you save the note.
about.edit: Write together, live. Nothing gets overwritten by accident.
about.freeze: Save a fixed copy keeps the note exactly as it is now, with a view-only link nobody can change. The original stays editable.
about.lead: Your note is locked in your browser before it’s saved. The key that opens it is part of the link you share, so we can’t read it: only people with the link can. Questions? See the FAQ.
about.links_h: What people with a link can do
about.links_p: One note can have many links: say, “Can write” for your team and “View only” for a client. Turn any link off at any time.
about.more: Technical details, privacy and developer tools are in the FAQ.
about.read: Share information, instructions or a secret.
about.s1t: The text stays in this tab.
about.s2t: With a key that only the link carries.
about.s3t: We can’t read it; we only know your rules, like when it should disappear.
about.s4t: The link unlocks it in their browser.
about.suggest: People propose changes; you see the difference and decide.
about.timed: Open later keeps a note closed until a time you choose. Stop changes turns writing links into view-only links at a set time.

faq.account_a: No. Without an account, your owner links are remembered in this browser. With an account, your notes appear under “My notes” on every device you sign in on.
faq.accounts_a: Your password never leaves your browser. It turns into two keys (PBKDF2, 600,000 rounds): one to sign in, and a vault key that encrypts your list of notes. With SSO sign-in, a vault phrase you choose plays that role. We can’t read your list either.
faq.accounts_q: How do accounts keep my notes private?
faq.away_a: A safety net for important information. The note stays closed while you keep opening it with your owner link; if you don’t for the number of days you chose, it opens for the people you gave a link to. Nothing is sent by email: they just need the link.
faq.cli_a: The notehop program encrypts on your computer: notehop new -server https://your-domain < note.md prints a link, and notehop get LINK prints the note. Same encryption as the browser.
faq.decoy_a: For notes with a password. A second password opens harmless text you write instead of the real note, and you can see when it was used. Both look the same to the server, so it can’t tell which is real.
faq.devices_a: Open your owner link on the other device (Share → Copy owner link), or sign in to the same account there. To let others write too, give them a “Can write” link.
faq.devices_q: How do I open my note on my other phone or computer?
faq.encrypt_a: Your browser locks the note with a random key before it’s saved (AES-256-GCM, end-to-end encryption). The key is the part of the link after #k=, and browsers never send that part to a server. So we store only scrambled data we can’t read.
faq.encrypt_q: How is my note kept private?
faq.files_a: Each file is locked in your browser with its own key before upload, and deleted from the server after 24 hours. Pasted images are made smaller (WebP) and lose hidden photo data such as location.
faq.fixed_a: “Save a fixed copy” keeps the note exactly as it is now, with its own view-only link that nobody can change, not even you. The original stays editable. Good for contracts and final versions.
faq.inbox_a: Turn it on to get an address. POST plain text, or JSON with text and from, and it’s added below the note. The server sees the text while it arrives and stores it sealed to the note’s key (P-256 + AES-GCM), so only link holders can read it. The Telegram bot can feed the same address: send it /connect followed by the address.
faq.later_a: “Open later” keeps the note closed until a time you choose; readers see a countdown and the server doesn’t send the content before then. “Stop changes” turns write, reply and tick links into view-only links at a set time; your owner link still works.
faq.later_q: Open later and Stop changes on a date
faq.lead: Short answers first; the technical details are here for anyone who wants them.
faq.leak_a: Open Share and turn that link off. It stops working right away; your other links keep working. If you turned on “Find out who leaked it”, paste the leaked text there to see which link it came from.
faq.leak_q: A link got into the wrong hands. What now?
faq.limits_a: Anyone with the full link can open the note, so treat the link like a password. Images from other websites aren’t loaded, so readers don’t leak to them. Features marked as public, or ones that receive text from other apps, mean the server sees that text.
faq.limits_q: What should I keep in mind?
faq.links_a: Each link has one permission: View only, Can write, Can reply (add below, can’t change), Can tick (tick the checklist) or Can suggest (you accept or reject). One note can have many links, and you can turn any of them off without affecting the others.
faq.links_q: What can people with a link do?
faq.lost_a: No, and that’s on purpose: the key to open the note is only in the link, so we never have it. Sign in to keep your links in your account, or save your owner link somewhere safe.
faq.lost_q: I lost the link. Can you get it back?
faq.mock_a: A public note that contains JSON (the whole text or a ```json block) is served at /mock/LINK, with paths like /mock/LINK/users/0 and open CORS, for prototypes.
faq.names_a: Random links have 10 characters and are practically impossible to guess. A name you choose needs at least 7 characters; shorter names and words like “help”, “admin” or brand names are reserved for the site. When a note is deleted or expires, its name is held for 90 days: only the same account can use it again in that time, so nobody can catch visitors of an old link. Offensive words aren’t allowed in link names or usernames.
faq.names_q: Link names: length, reserved names, reuse
faq.networks_a: Lets only listed IP addresses or networks (e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 10.0.0.0/8) open or change the note, for example your office. Your owner link always works.
faq.offline_a: Notes you opened before can be read offline, and NoteHop can be installed like an app. What’s kept on your device is the locked version; the key stays in your link. Notes set to delete after reading are never kept. Changes need a connection.
faq.once_a: The note is deleted after it has been opened the number of times you chose. Chat apps like WhatsApp and Telegram open links to make previews; the button makes sure only a person opening it counts.
faq.once_q: How does “Read once” work? Why is there a button before the note opens?
faq.owner_a: The link that ends with &a=…. It can change everything, add or turn off links, save fixed copies and delete the note. Treat it like a house key: don’t send it to others.
faq.page_a: Public notes saved in your account can be listed on /@your-name by turning on “Show on my public page”. Only view-only links are shown.
faq.password_a: When the link itself might be seen by others, e.g. in a shared chat. Readers then need the link and the password. Send the password another way. Technically the key becomes PBKDF2 (310,000 rounds) of the password and the link key.
faq.password_q: When should I add a password?
faq.public_a: A note with “Keep it private” turned off. It isn’t encrypted: anyone with the address can read it, the server can too, and it can be fetched as plain text with /raw/. Use it for things meant for everyone. Some features only work with public notes: your public page, the mock API and SSH.
faq.raw_a: Public notes can be fetched as plain text, e.g. curl https://your-domain/raw/note-name. Private notes can’t: the server doesn’t have the key.
faq.replies_a: Share a “Can reply” link: people add their reply below with their name and time, and can’t change anything else. For questions with fields, type /form in the editor.
faq.replies_q: How do I collect answers or replies?
faq.sees_a: Not your text, titles or file contents. It does see what it needs to enforce your choices: when a note was made and changed, its size, link permissions, expiry, how many times it was opened, which boxes are ticked and how many votes a poll has (not the labels), and IP addresses for abuse limits.
faq.sign_a: Readers can sign the current version with their name. The first signature on a version saves a fixed copy of it, so everyone can see exactly what was signed.
faq.ssh_a: If the server has it turned on, ssh -p 2222 your-domain < note.md creates a public note (kept 30 days) and ssh -p 2222 your-domain get LINK prints one. Public notes only.
faq.title: Questions & answers
faq.together_a: Yes. With a “Can write” link, everyone sees each other’s typing and names live, and there’s a chat on the side. Chat messages are private and are never saved: they disappear when everyone leaves.
faq.together_q: Can several people write at the same time?
faq.trace_a: When it’s on, text copied from the note carries invisible characters that identify the link it was copied through. Paste leaked text into the box in Share to see which link it was. Someone who knows about it can remove the marks.
faq.watch_a: NoteHop sends a POST to your https address a few seconds after changes: {"note":"…","events":["updated","entry"],"version":7,"time":…}, never the text. Check the X-NoteHop-Signature: sha256=… header (HMAC-SHA256 of the body with the key shown in the settings). Private addresses are refused.
faq.watch_q: Notify my app when it changes
faq.what_a: A place to write a note and share it with a link. You decide what people with the link can do: read it, write with you, reply, tick a list, or suggest changes. Notes are private by default.

privacy.lead: We built NoteHop so we can’t read your private notes. Here is what we do keep, and why.
privacy.s1: The text, titles and files of private notes. They are locked in your browser; the key is in your link and never reaches us.
privacy.s2: Locked notes, link permissions, times, how often a note was opened, ticks and poll counts, and, if you have an account, your username and an encrypted list of your notes.
privacy.s3: Your IP address is used to limit abuse (rate limits and network limits you set) and appears in short-lived server logs. We don’t sell data and use no ads or third-party trackers.
privacy.s4: One cookie keeps you signed in and one remembers your language. Your browser also keeps your owner links, drafts of settings and offline copies on your device; you can clear them any time.
privacy.s5: Public notes, SSH, the mock API, the inbox and the Telegram bot mean the server sees that text. They are marked in the app and explained in the FAQ.
privacy.s5_h: Features where the server sees text
privacy.s6: Delete a note with its owner link and it’s removed right away; expired notes are removed within a minute. Server backups are kept for a limited time (14 days by default) and then deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy

terms.lead: The short version: use NoteHop for lawful things, keep your links safe, and know that we can’t read private notes.
terms.s1: You may use NoteHop to write and share notes. Don’t use it for anything illegal, to harass people, to spread malware or phishing, or to share content you have no right to share.
terms.s2: Your notes stay yours. Private notes are locked in your browser, so we can’t read, check or recover them. You’re responsible for what you write and who you give links to.
terms.s3: We may remove a note or turn off a link when we learn it breaks these terms or the law, for example a public note used for phishing. Because we can’t read private notes, we act on the link that was reported.
terms.s4: We do our best to keep NoteHop running, but it’s provided as is. Keep copies of anything important: notes that expire, read-once notes and attachments disappear by design.
terms.s5: Names you choose need at least 7 characters. Some names are reserved for the site, offensive names aren’t allowed, and the name of a deleted note is held for 90 days. We may take back a name that impersonates someone.
terms.s6: We may update these terms; the version below shows which one this is. Questions? See the contact page.
terms.title: Terms of use
tg.bad_inbox: That inbox address doesn’t work (turned off or mistyped).
tg.connected: Connected. Your next messages will be added to the note.
tg.disconnected: Disconnected. Messages are no longer saved.
tg.help:
NoteHop bot: send messages into a note.

1. Open your note, Share → Advanced settings → Inbox, and copy the address.
2. Send here: /connect https://…/in/…
3. Every message you send after that is added to the note (stored encrypted).

/disconnect stops it. Note: Telegram and the NoteHop server see these messages while they travel.
tg.not_connected: This chat isn’t linked to a note yet. Send /help to see how.

timed.open_off: Off. Pick a time: until then nobody can read it, and readers see a countdown.

vault.create_lead: You signed in with SSO, so NoteHop doesn't know your password. Create a phrase to encrypt the list of notes in your account. You'll be asked for it again on new devices. If you forget it, the list can't be opened, not even by us.
vault.hint: At least 8 characters. A few words are safer and easier to remember.
vault.open_lead: Enter the vault key you created on NoteHop. It unlocks the titles and links of the notes in your account and is never sent to the server.
warn.public_keys: This public note contains a private link or attachment key (#k=… or nh-file:…). Anyone who can read this note could open those too. Continue anyway?
watch.off: Off. Your app gets a message when the note changes: what changed and when, never the text.
watch.on: On: we notify {url} when the note changes. Signing key: {key}
watermark.off: Off. Text copied from this note can carry an invisible mark of the link it came from, so you can tell which link leaked it.
watermark.on: On: copied text carries an invisible mark of its link. Paste leaked text below to check.
